body:
sarah_support: Hey team — multiple priority-1 customers (IDs: cust-42, cust-77) are reporting 502/504 errors and timeouts hitting the hosted inference API in us-west-2a since ~2026-03-15T09:12Z. Also seeing a bunch of auth failures in the support logs where user requests return 401s during the same window. Raising an incident because customers are escalating to account teams.

zane_network_eng: Thanks Sarah. I see elevated packet loss and cross-AZ latency spikes from our edge probes to us-west-2a. Packet loss ~8-15% for some traces, RTT jumping 40-200ms intermittently. AWS peering graph shows flaps on one transit peer.

tia_reliability: Correlating with Redwood gateway logs — multiple upstream gateway pools returning 502, with a surge of internal proxy timeouts at the same minutes. SLO alarms triggered for 95p latency.

oliver_support: Customers report they can still hit other regions (eu1) fine — only us-west-2a is affected. Also one customer called saying billing webhook retries started failing too (webhook endpoint got 504s). Not sure if billing system is on same infra route.

mjensen: Can we get the deploy/gateway health logs? infra-bot, any recent config changes?

infra-bot: Deploy window check: no gateway config deploys in the last 4 hours. Last gateway change was 2026-03-14. No autoscaler flaps.

deploy-bot: Canary probes show 5xx spike starting 09:11:38Z. Route table change event recorded for transit-peer-3 at 09:10:59Z from provider.

zane_network_eng: I pulled traceroutes and mtr to the affected AZ. Sample output (sanitized):
```
mtr -r -c 30 api-usw2a-edge
 1. 10.1.0.1 0.6% 1ms
 2. 198.51.100.9 0.0% 12ms
 3. 203.0.113.5 12.3% 48ms  <-- packet loss starts
 4. 198.51.200.22 9.7% 82ms
 5. x.x.x.x (transit-peer-3) 14.6% 150ms
 6. api-gateway-usw2a 0.0% 160ms (sporadic)
```
Looks like a provider path micro-loss on transit-peer-3. BGP updates show a flap and quick withdraw/announce pattern.

tia_reliability: From the product side, the token validator service (auth-svc) in us-west-2a is timing out intermittently when it calls the internal IAM store — causing our frontends to return 401 in some flows where auth validation fails after retry. That likely explains the auth noise. Log snippet:
```
[09:12:01Z] auth-svc timeout calling iam-store: context deadline exceeded
[09:12:01Z] auth-svc returning 502->frontend (t=1200ms)
```

sarah_support: Customers want repro steps so they can confirm. Can we provide a minimal curl they can run? Also need ETA for mitigation.

mjensen: Repro curl: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate` — affected customers will see 502/504 or 401. But note: if they have region pinned to eu1, they won't see it.

oliver_support: I posted that repro to the ticket queue and asked customers to try with region override header `X-Redwood-Region: eu1` as a temporary workaround. Some customers confirmed it works. :thumbsup:

zane_network_eng: Short-term mitigation we can do from our side: 1) Shift traffic off transit-peer-3 (apply BGP weight/localpref to prefer alternate peer) 2) Enable cross-AZ failover for gateway NLB to route around the impaired path 3) Increase auth-svc retry/backoff to avoid turning transient network errors into hard 401s. I'm starting step 1 now and opening a provider ticket.

tia_reliability: I'm going to scale up auth-svc in that AZ and enable an aggressive retry with jitter locally so token validation is more resilient while we wait for the provider. Rolling config now (no user-facing deploy).

infra-bot: BGP weight change applied to transit-peer-3: set localpref -100 for prefix set PFX-RED-EDGE at 09:20:12Z. Monitoring for convergence.

deploy-bot: NLB cross-zone failover enabling rollout started at 09:21:04Z (progress: 30%). Will report when 100%.

aws-peering-bot: Provider ticket created INC-9983: reported intermittent packet loss on path to us-west-2a via transit-peer-3. Provider acknowledged and is investigating. Ticket link: https://provider.example/ticket/INC-9983

zane_network_eng: After localpref change, preliminary probes show packet loss dropping to ~1-2% and 5xx rate halved. Still seeing occasional spikes while BGP converges.

tia_reliability: Auth-svc replicas scaled +2, local retry config applied. 401s in logs fell by ~80% post-scale.

oliver_support: Customer cust-42 confirmed service restored at 09:28Z after we recommended region override and we applied routing changes. They reopened their ticket and marked ‘partial resolution’.

sarah_support: Good — customers still want a post-incident writeup and explanation of root cause. Also request from compliance: were any auth tokens leaked or retried excessively?

mjensen: No evidence of token leaks. The auth errors were from timeouts and the frontend returning auth-failure paths. We should audit token retry counts for the window (09:10-09:40Z).

zane_network_eng: Provider says they saw a flapping interface causing microbursts on that egress path; they did a hard interface reset and claim full restoration at 09:31Z. We're continuing to monitor for late jitter.

tia_reliability: Next actions: 1) postmortem runbook entry for cross-AZ provider flaps 2) add canary that checks auth-svc validate latency and treats >700ms as degraded 3) investigate if billing webhook traffic needs separate routing or retries.

oliver_support: I'll close customer-facing tickets with a note about the temporary route failover + provider fix and offer to assist with region override if they need it.

sarah_support: Thanks all. Marking incident as mitigated at 09:31Z but keeping channel open for follow-ups. Will draft postmortem and tag infra/ops for RCA. :white_check_mark:
